arxiv-1504-04034.title: Non-Zero θ 13 \theta_{13} and δ C ​ P \delta_{CP} in a Neutrino Mass Model with A 4 A_{4} Symmetry
arxiv-1504-04034.creator: Abhish Dev, P. Ramadevi, and S. Uma Sankar
arxiv-1504-04034.description: A 2015 arXiv research paper by Abhish Dev, P. Ramadevi, and S. Uma Sankar. In this paper, we consider a neutrino mass model based on A 4 A_{4} symmetry. The spontaneous symmetry breaking in this model is chosen to obtain tribimaximal mixing in the neutrino sector. We introduce Z 2 × Z 2 Z_{2}\times Z_{2} invariant perturbations in this model which can give rise to acceptable values of θ 13 \theta_{13} and δ C ​ P \delta_{CP} .

arxiv-1902-07598.title: Search for heavy neutrinos with the T2K near detector ND280
arxiv-1902-07598.creator: K. Abe, R. Akutsu, A. Ali, C. Andreopoulos, L. Anthony, M. Antonova, S. Aoki, A. Ariga, Y. Ashida, Y. Awataguchi, Y. Azuma, S. Ban, M. Barbi, G.J. Barker, G. Barr, C. Barry, M. Batkiewicz-Kwasniak, F. Bench, V. Berardi, S. Berkman, R.M. Berner, L. Berns, S. Bhadra, S. Bienstock, A. Blondel, S. Bolog
arxiv-1902-07598.description: Abstract This paper reports on the search for heavy neutrinos with masses in the range 140 < M N < 493 140<M_{N}<493 MeV/c 2 using the off-axis near detector ND280 of the T2K experiment. These particles can be produced from kaon decays in the standard neutrino beam and then subsequently decay in ND280.

arxiv-2107-07451.title: Data vs classifiers, who wins?
arxiv-2107-07451.creator: Lucas Cardoso, Vitor Santos, Regiane Francês, Ricardo Prudêncio, Ronnie Alves
arxiv-2107-07451.description: Abstract The experiments covered by Machine Learning (ML) must consider two important aspects to assess the performance of a model: datasets and algorithms. Robust benchmarks are needed to evaluate the best classifiers. For this, one can adopt gold standard benchmarks available in public repositories. However, it is common not to consider the complexity of the dataset when evaluating.

arxiv-2205-14256.title: The Common Envelope Evolution Outcome—A Case Study on Hot Subdwarf B Stars
arxiv-2205-14256.creator: Hongwei Ge, Christopher A Tout, Xuefei Chen, Matthias U Kruckow, Hailiang Chen, Dengkai Jiang, Zhenwei Li, Zhengwei Liu, Zhanwen Han
arxiv-2205-14256.description: Abstract Common envelope evolution (CEE) physics plays a fundamental role in the formation of binary systems, such as mergering stellar gravitational wave sources, pulsar binaries and type Ia supernovae. A precisely constrained CEE has become more important in the age of large surveys and gravitational wave detectors.

arxiv-2206-14343.title: State space model multiple imputation for missing data in non-stationary multivariate time series with application in digital Psychiatry
arxiv-2206-14343.creator: Xiaoxuan Cai, Xinru Wang, Li Zeng, Habiballah Rahimi Eichi, Dost Ongur, Lisa Dixon
arxiv-2206-14343.description: Abstract Mobile technology (e.g., mobile phones and wearable devices) provides effective and scalable methods for collecting physiological and behavioral biomarkers in patients’ naturalistic settings, as well as opportunity for therapeutic advancements and scientific discoveries regarding the etiology of psychiatric illness. Continuous data collection yields a new type of data: entangled multivariate time series of outcome, exposure, and covariates.

arxiv-2207-00673.title: Perspectives and Opportunities: A Molecular Toolkit for Fundamental Physics and Matter Wave Interferometry in Microgravity A portion of this research was carried out at the Jet Propulsion Laboratory, California Institute of Technology, under a contract with the National Aeronautics and Space Adminis

Efremov, Stefan Nimmrichter, Björn Schrinski, Ethan Elliott, Wolfgang Ketterle. The study of molecular physics using ultracold gases has provided a unique probe into the fundamental properties of nature and offers new tools for quantum technologies.

arxiv-2309-07550.title: Naturalistic Robot Arm Trajectory Generation via Representation Learning
arxiv-2309-07550.creator: Jayjun Lee, Adam J. Spiers
arxiv-2309-07550.description: Abstract The integration of manipulator robots in household environments suggests a need for more predictable and human-like robot motion. This holds especially true for wheelchair-mounted assistive robots that can support the independence of people with paralysis. One method of generating naturalistic motion trajectories is via the imitation of human demonstrators.

arxiv-2310-17135.title: COMPARISON OF CROSS-ENTROPY, DICE, AND FOCAL LOSS FOR SEA ICE TYPE SEGMENTATION
arxiv-2310-17135.creator: Rafael Pires de Lima, Behzad Vahedi, Morteza Karimzadeh
arxiv-2310-17135.description: Abstract † † address: 1 Department of Geography, University of Colorado Boulder Up-to-date sea ice charts are crucial for safer navigation in ice-infested waters. Recently, Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) models show the potential to accelerate the generation of ice maps for large regions.

arxiv-2508-19464.title: Bridging Language Gaps: Enhancing Few-Shot Language Adaptation
arxiv-2508-19464.creator: Philipp Borchert, Jochen De Weerdt, Marie-Francine Moens
arxiv-2508-19464.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Philipp Borchert, Jochen De Weerdt, Marie-Francine Moens. The disparity in language resources poses a challenge in multilingual NLP, with high-resource languages benefiting from extensive data, while low-resource languages lack sufficient data for effective training. Our Co ntrastive L anguage A lignment with P rompting ( CoLAP ) method addresses this gap by integrating contrastive learning with cross-lingual representations, facilitating task-specific knowledge transfer from high-resource to lower-resource languages.

arxiv-2602-07840.title: SAGE: Scalable AI Governance & Evaluation Conference: Preprint; 2025; Preprint
arxiv-2602-07840.creator: Benjamin Le, Xueying Lu, Nick Stern, Wenqiong Liu, Igor Lapchuk, Xiang Li, Baofen Zheng, Kevin Rosenberg, Jiewen Huang, Zhe Zhang, Abraham Cabangbang, Satej Milind Wagle, Jianqiang Shen, Raghavan Muthuregunathan, Abhinav Gupta, Mathew Teoh, Andrew Kirk, Thomas Kwan, Jingwei Wu, Wenjing Zhang
arxiv-2602-07840.description: Abstract . Evaluating relevance in large-scale search systems is fundamentally constrained by the governance gap between nuanced, resource-constrained human oversight and the high-throughput requirements of production systems. While traditional approaches rely on engagement proxies or sparse manual review, these methods often fail to capture the full scope of high-impact relevance failures.

pmc-11504872.title: Managerial Influence on Infection Prevention and Control (IPC) Implementation in Israeli Hospitals: A Doctoral Research Study
pmc-11504872.creator: Dafna Chen, Stefan Cojocaru
pmc-11504872.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Background: This research, part of a doctoral study, aims to examine the impact of managerial factors on the implementation of Infection Prevention and Control (IPC) measures in Israeli hospitals. The study focuses on identifying key facilitators and barriers from the perspectives of physician and nurse managers, with an emphasis on understanding the integration of managerial strategies and theoretical frameworks in IPC implementation. Objective: The objective is to explore specific managerial factors, both facilitators and barriers, influencing the effective implementation of IPC measures.

pmc-11661403.title: Impact of Reverse Empowerment and Proactive Motivations on Physicians’ Online Knowledge Sharing in Digital Platforms: Survey Study
pmc-11661403.creator: Jingyuan Su, Kathy Ning Shen, Xitong Guo, Amy Schwartz, Hyorim Ju, Seyyed Babak Alavi
pmc-11661403.description: BackgroundDigital platforms offer a venue for patients and physicians to exchange health information and provide health care services outside traditional organizational contexts. Previous studies have seldom focused on the factors that drive the proactivity of physicians’ online behavior. Additionally, there is limited research exploring the influence of patients on physicians’ online behavior, particularly from the perspective of patients possessing power.

pmc-12411799.title: Clinical Significance, Differential Diagnosis and Initial Management of Hematuria in Emergency and Outpatient Settings
pmc-12411799.creator: Stanislaw Szymkiewicz
pmc-12411799.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Hematuria is a common clinical symptom that may reflect a wide spectrum of underlying conditions, ranging from benign etiologies to potentially life-threatening diseases such as urothelial carcinoma or renal trauma. It is generally classified as either gross (visible) or microscopic (detected only through urinalysis), and particularly in emergency settings, it requires prompt and structured evaluation to guide further diagnostic and therapeutic decisions.

pmc-12654475.title: Enhancing Shear Performance of Concrete Beams Using Layered Rubberized and Steel Fiber-Reinforced Composites
pmc-12654475.creator: Abdulaziz S. Alsaif, Abdulrahman S. Albidah
pmc-12654475.description: Recycling rubber and steel fibers from end-of-life tires for use in structural concrete presents a sustainable pathway to improve resource efficiency and reduce environmental impact. This study assesses the shear performance of reinforced concrete beams in which shredded tire rubber substitutes 20 vol.% of both fine and coarse natural aggregates.

pmc-12831388.title: Conservative management of postoperative incomplete lung torsion without reoperation: first case report with 2-year favorable outcomes
pmc-12831388.creator: Keyao Dai, Yuan Zhang, Yudong Zhang, Yucong Deng, Shen Lao, Wei Wang
pmc-12831388.description: BackgroundLung torsion is a rare but serious postoperative complication in thoracic surgery, with traditional management requiring surgical intervention such as video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery or open thoracotomy. Reoperation carries significantly higher mortality rates and prolonged hospitalization compared to routine surgical outcomes. To date, no cases of successful conservative management of postoperative lung torsion have been reported in the literature.

pmc-13083032.title: A carbon monoxide cycle drives carbon monoxide uptake and poisoning
pmc-13083032.creator: Ronald F Coburn, Michael S Tift
pmc-13083032.description: An understanding of the physiology of acute carbon monoxide (CO) poisoning remains incomplete. This study describes a novel approach—considering a CO cycle driven by CO inhalation which includes: alveolar CO uptake → the transport to peripheral tissues → an increase in the PCO and [COHb] in peripheral capillary blood → and a return of COHb to the lungs.

pmc-13103659.title: Lower limb amputation in incident dialysis patients in England: incidence, outcomes and inter-centre variation from a national registry study
pmc-13103659.creator: Nithin Bodapati, Sherry Masoud, Javeria Peracha, David Pitcher, Anna Casula, Retha Steenkamp, James Medcalf, Dorothea Nitsch, Gerry Rayman, William McKane, Graham Lipkin
pmc-13103659.description: BackgroundLower limb amputation (LLA) is a devastating complication in dialysis patients, often related to diabetes and peripheral vascular disease. National data on LLA incidence, variation and outcomes in England are limited.MethodsA retrospective cohort study conducted using linked data from the UK Renal Registry (UKRR) and Hospital Episode Statistics for incident dialysis patients in England (2003–17).

pmc-13222398.title: Sex differences in cardiovascular disease risk in type 1 diabetes: The vascular bed paradox in women
pmc-13222398.creator: Abigayle B Simon, Dhruti Trivedi, Marsha Blackburn, Jeffrey Thomas, Matthew S Nicholson, Lawrence C Layman, Ryan A Harris
pmc-13222398.description: BackgroundCardiovascular disease (CVD) is the leading cause of death in individuals with type 1 diabetes (T1D). Epidemiological studies indicate that women with T1D are at greater risk of CVD compared to men with T1D. The present study sought to investigate differences in vascular health between men and women with T1D.
